structural_root_cause.asymmetry_in_bridge: V8.1 introduced _canonicalize_challenger_payload (plan_convergence_bridge.py:428) to wrap agent's plan_content into the kernel challenger contract — synthesizing source_revision_id + source_plan_content_hash from authoritative plan_convergence state. The PRIMARY revision dispatch (round-2+ revision after cross-review verdict) had NO equivalent canonicalizer: record_plan_result's record_revision arm at line 192-198 passed `details.revision or details.plan or details` straight to record_revision. _validate_revision requires revision_id + round + content + content_hash + parent_revision_hash — kernel-state-derived fields the agent has no read access to.
structural_root_cause.lesson: Bridge canonicalizers are the architectural seam between agent-emitted shape (canonical 7-field plan_content) and kernel state machine shape (revision metadata + content hashes + state-anchored ids). Every role that mints a kernel state transition needs a canonicalizer; the absence of one is a kernel bug, NOT an agent contract drift.
structural_root_cause.tier_1_anchor: Different bug class from F-018/F-019/F-020 — those were SSoT/agent prompt drift. F-021 is BRIDGE MECHANICS — the kernel-side seam that translates agent canonical output into kernel state machine inputs was incomplete for the primary-revision path. The fix is symmetric: mirror _canonicalize_challenger_payload.

tier_1_architectural_fix.scope: kernel bridge symmetry — primary-revision canonicalizer mirrors challenger canonicalizer
files_changed: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/plan_convergence_bridge.py (new _canonicalize_revision_payload helper + record_plan_result.record_revision dispatch now routes through it)

aria-kernel/tests/invariants/v10/test_phase_v10_4_phase_3_h_10_primary_revision_canonicalizer.py (5 Tier-3 invariants — existence, kernel-state read, required-field synthesis, dispatch routing, end-to-end smoke)
tier_1_architectural_fix.tier_rationale: Tier-1 (make impossible): the kernel synthesizes revision_id + content_hash + parent_revision_hash from authoritative plan_convergence state; the agent contract stays narrow (plan_content only). Agent has no read access to kernel state, so any agent-supplied value is ignored in favour of the kernel-derived value. This eliminates the F-021 failure surface AND the structurally-related risk that a malicious agent could craft a state-rewrite via revision metadata. Tier-3 (make detectable): 5 invariants catch any future regression of the bridge symmetry.

agent_prompt_changes: NONE — aria-primary-planner.md keeps emitting plan_content only. The architectural simplification is that revision metadata is kernel-owned.

expected_impact_on_endurance.before_fix: cycle 4+ all blocked at CROSS_REVIEWED state. Round-2 primary subprocess runs, outer envelope accepted, bridge fold fails. Plan never advances past round 1's CROSS_REVIEWED → eventual cross_review_poll_timeout → convergence_blocked. No round-2 challenger, no round-2 cross_review, no verdict derivation, no convergence_resolved, no implementation_requested.
expected_impact_on_endurance.after_fix: next round-2 primary subprocess hot-reload picks up updated bridge. Round-2 revision recorded → state advances to CRITIQUED (or back to some pre-revision state per state machine) → next round's challenger spawns → next round's cross_review → eventual verdict (CONVERGED or HUMAN_REQUIRED). For CONVERGED verdict: implementation_requested fires, ARIA spawns aria-implementer, opens a real PR. This is the first chance to observe the FULL convergence pipeline end-to-end.
